document.title: Speed up review generation: directory refs and a leaner skill
document.summary: A hunk ref can name a directory, so the digest and draft of a large PR shrink to one line per mechanical directory, and the skill runs in three tool calls with sources, log, and validate folded into them.
document.why: [Reviews take too long and spend too many tokens on the medium and small PRs that make up most of the reports](source:s1), and on a 190-file PR [the step-2 output got truncated](source:s2).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 2026
sources.gist: Máté asked to speed up review generation, then to focus on medium and small PRs with speed and token use as the metrics, to review the skill text for a smaller model, and to make it work with Haiku 5.5.

sources.label: Directory hunk refs; sources ride in the step-2 call
sources.gist: A ref ending in / covers a directory; the digest collapses a mechanical directory with at least five pure renames; the draft holds one path per file; the step-2 output no longer gets truncated.

sources.label: Directory refs: the most specific ref wins
sources.gist: Fixes from review: a path ref beats a directory ref, validate fails a non-mechanical file under a directory ref, refresh drafts new hunks under a directory ref, old-side pins on renamed files, the What changed page lists directory files, collapse needs half the files to be pure renames.

sources.label: Skill: apply the writing review
sources.gist: Steps in run order, one fetch rule, pins defined by base and head file, a PR comment is a source only when cited or pinned, duplicated rules gone.

sources.label: Digest: 'same change as', not 'identical copy'; sources capped at 10 kB
sources.gist: The mirrors hint marks the same added and removed lines, not identical files; Claude Code shows at most 30 kB of one shell result.

lookFor: [The first directory-ref commit](source:s2) collapses a directory with at least five pure renames; [the follow-up](source:s3) changes that rule to at least half of the directory's files, and the skill text says the same.

[The session asked for speed and token use on medium and small PRs](source:s1). Measured on the eval cases, the skill changes give about 1.3x on small PRs and the directory refs cut a 190-file digest to a third; the writing rewrite itself is speed-neutral and holds the graded quality.

parts.name: Directory refs
parts.summary: A ref ending in / covers every live hunk under that directory, through schema, coverage, refresh, the UI, and the eval checks.

parts.name: Skill rewrite
parts.summary: The skill reads sources in the step-2 call, groups and fetches in one call, writes and validates in one call, and names the lookFor fields in the write step.

groups.title: A hunk ref can be a directory
groups.why: Coverage, refresh, the UI, and the eval checks all read refs through this contract, so it comes first.
groups.summary: `DirHunkRef` joins `ReviewHunkRef` in `identity.ts`, `refCoversPath` says whether one ref covers a path, `groupsHoldingPath` says which groups hold a path (a path or hunk ref beats a directory ref, the deepest directory wins), and the schema in `review.ts` accepts a string ending in `/`.

groups.title: Coverage: the most specific ref wins
groups.why: A directory ref must not swallow a file another group names, and must not hide a file with a real change; [the review of the first commit asked for both](source:s3).
groups.summary: `dirOwners` in `coverage.ts` gives each live hunk to the path ref that names it, else to the deepest directory ref, and `dirRefErrors` fails a directory ref that holds a file that is not mechanical; `checks.ts` applies `groupsHoldingPath` for the eval together and apart checks, and the server and covering-document tests carry a directory ref.
lookFor: Subtle: a path or hunk ref in any group takes the file out of every directory ref; a file named in two groups is still counted once per group, and a directory ref whose files are all named elsewhere matches nothing and is reported stale.

groups.title: Digest and draft collapse a mechanical directory
groups.why: [The 190-file digest was 27 kB and the draft 23 kB, past what one tool result shows](source:s2); one line per mechanical directory brings them to a third.
groups.summary: `mechanicalDirs` in `digest.ts` finds a directory whose changed files are all mechanical with at least half pure renames and prints it as one `DigestDir` line, `pregroup` in `commands.ts` writes it as one `dir/` ref and one path per other file, and the `mirrorOf` hint reads `same change as` because [it marks the same added and removed lines, not an identical file](source:s5).

groups.title: Refresh keeps a directory ref
groups.why: A refreshed review must carry a directory ref over to new commits without losing the files that appeared under it.
groups.summary: `refreshDocument` in `refresh.ts` keeps a directory ref whose directory still has live hunks, reports the changed and reformatted hunks under it, and leaves new files under it to the `update` group.
lookFor: Subtle: a directory ref collects `changed` and `reformat` hunks of the files it covers but not `newHunks`; a file added under that directory at the new head lands in the draft `update` group, where a path ref would have kept it.

groups.title: Pins on renamed files and the What changed list
groups.why: An old-side comment pin names the base path, which no directory ref at head covers; [the review asked that it still find its group](source:s3).
groups.summary: `groupIdForPinnedSource` in `source.ts` finds a pin's group through `groupsHoldingPath`, after `App.tsx` maps an `old` pin on a renamed file to its head path; the API file entry carries `relocation` so a copy stays out of that map, and `groupPaths` in `changes.ts` lists on the What changed page only the files a directory ref holds under the same rule.
lookFor: Subtle: only a pin with `side` `old` goes through the rename map, and a copy's old path is not in it; a `new` pin on the old path of a renamed file matches no ref and falls back to the groups that list the source id.

groups.title: Schema JSON copies
groups.why: The built schema and its two skill copies change the one description string together.
groups.summary: The same one-line description of a hunk ref repeats in three generated JSON files; read one, skip the rest.

groups.title: The skill in three tool calls
groups.why: [Every extra round trip re-sends the whole context, and the 40-line source cap cut the comments the model needed](source:s2); [the writing review removed duplicated rules and put the steps in run order](source:s4).
groups.summary: `skills-next/comprehende/SKILL.md` folds the source reads and `git log base..head` into the step-2 call, groups and fetches in one `show` call, writes `review.json` with a heredoc that ends in `validate`, names both `lookFor` fields in the write step, and caps each source at 10 kB; the `.agents` copies repeat it, `example.md` keeps the draft's `source` object, `skill.test.ts` and `skill-sync.test.ts` pin the wording, and the `Do not run that command` sentence stays because `install-local-skill.ts` rewrites it.

commits.subject: One path-ownership rule for pins, What changed, and eval checks
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
groupsHoldingPath in identity.ts says which groups hold a path: a path or hunk ref in any group beats a directory ref, and the deepest directory wins. Pin lookup, the What changed file list, and the eval together/apart checks use it instead of three partial copies. The pin rename map skips copies: the API file entry now carries relocation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Skill: keep the 'Do not run that command' sentence
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The writing review dropped it as a negation, but install-local-skill.ts rewrites that sentence and the sync test pins it. The refresh pin follows the reworded rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Digest: 'same change as', not 'identical copy'; sources capped at 10 kB
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The mirrors hint marks files that received the same added and removed lines, not identical files. Both producers wrote 'identical, skip it' for two different files and the grader flagged it. The CLI, the draft group text, and the skill now say the change repeats. The source cap drops to 10 kB per file: Claude Code shows at most 30 kB of one shell result, and 16 kB files pushed the step-2 call past it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Skill: the write step names both lookFor fields
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The graded comparison showed zero lookFor bullets after the rewrite on the two cases whose claims are behavior traces. Step 4 now checks source items against the fetched hunks for document lookFor, and asks for a group lookFor bullet where a fetched hunk hides a behavior change, with both in its Done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Skill: apply the writing review
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Steps are in the order the run takes: group and fetch, then write. The field shape keeps the draft's source object, so refresh accepts the document. Steps 2 and 3 are one call with one Done. One fetch rule, in one place. Pins are defined by base and head file, with GitHub as the example. A PR comment is a source only when the prose cites it or it gets a pin. Duplicated rules, negations that restate a positive rule, and sentences with no action are gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Skill: a digest of up to six files fetches every readable file
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The fetch budget was weighed on every change, including two-file ones. Small digests now fetch every file that is not mechanical or a copy, with no decision; the budget rule applies past six files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Skill: read sources whole, log base..head, validate in the write call
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Sources are read with a byte cap instead of 40 lines; the 40-line cap cut the comment files of half the eval cases and the model reasoned about what it could not see. The commit log is base..head: the symmetric difference printed commits from main that are not in the change. review.json is written with a heredoc and validated in the same shell call, one step fewer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Directory refs: the most specific ref wins
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Fixes from review of the directory-ref change:
- A path or hunk ref in any group takes its file out of a directory ref, and
  the deepest directory ref wins over a shallower one. A file the draft
  collapsed can move to its story by naming its path there.
- validate fails a directory ref that holds a file that is not mechanical.
- refresh drafts every new hunk under a directory ref into the update group.
- An old-side PR comment pin on a renamed file finds the group whose
  directory ref holds the new path.
- The What-changed page lists the files a directory ref holds.
- A directory collapses only when at least half its files are pure renames.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Directory hunk refs; sources ride in the step-2 call
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A ref ending in / covers every live hunk under that directory. The digest
collapses a directory whose changed files are all mechanical, with at least
five pure renames, into one line, and pregroup writes it as one ref. The draft
now holds one path per file instead of one ref per hunk. On a 190-file PR the
digest shrinks from 27KB to 9KB and the draft from 23KB to 2.5KB, so the
step-2 output no longer gets truncated.

Digest hunk refs of renamed files now carry the old path, so a copied ref
matches live git.

The skill folds the source reads into the step-2 shell call and drops
git diff --stat, which the digest already covers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
